editorial_candidates.source_claim: The heat ball E_r(t,x) is a compact backward space-time region whose slices at depth tau are closed balls of radius rho_n(tau), shrink to the top point, attain maximal radius at tau=r^2/(4 pi e), and are empty beyond tau=r^2/(4 pi) (Statement lines 47–61).
editorial_candidates.why_warranted: The definition is explicitly geometric and the varying spatial slices encode the heat-kernel level set; a small space-time sketch would make the slice formula and unique top point easier to parse.
editorial_candidates.content_to_draw_or_check: Draw t vertical and one spatial coordinate horizontal (label the n-dimensional slice as a ball); mark the top (x,t), the slice at depth tau as B(x,rho_n(tau)), the point slice at tau=r^2/(4pi), the empty region below it, and the widest slice at tau=r^2/(4pi e). Preserve the stated direction of time and avoid depicting an exact Euclidean sphere in n+1 dimensions.
editorial_candidates.limitation: The formula is fully stated and proved algebraically; this would be explanatory only.

editorial_candidates.source_claim: The free wave value at (x,t) depends only on initial data on the closed ball B_ct(x), while the forced value depends only on the source in the backward cone 0<=s<=t, |y-x|<=c(t-s) (Statement line 35; Proof line 57).
editorial_candidates.why_warranted: These two related domains of dependence are central to the claim and naturally spatial in space-time.
editorial_candidates.content_to_draw_or_check: Draw the apex (x,t), the backward cone with slopes +/-1/c, its t=0 base interval [x-ct,x+ct], and in an adjacent spatial slice the ball B_ct(x); label initial data on the base and source inside the cone. Keep the cone’s sides and inclusion inequality consistent with |y-x|<=c(t-s).
editorial_candidates.limitation: A schematic may complement the explicit formulas; it is not required for the local determination proof.

editorial_candidates.source_claim: The characteristic map X_t(y)=y-t arctan(y) remains increasing for t<1, loses a nonzero derivative at y=0,t=1 while the solution remains continuous, and for t>1 characteristics from y=+/-a(t) meet at the stationary entropy shock x=0 (Statement lines 35–45).
editorial_candidates.why_warranted: The before/at/after transition is the example’s main point and is encoded by the characteristic geometry.
editorial_candidates.content_to_draw_or_check: Use an x–t plot with characteristic curves labelled by y, showing the first tangency/gradient blow-up at (0,1), and for t>1 the symmetric incoming labels +/-a(t) meeting at the stationary shock x=0. Optionally pair with profiles u(t,x) at t<1, t=1, t>1; keep the shock traces u^-=arctan(a), u^+=-arctan(a) and distinguish the continuous t=1 cusp from the postcritical jump.
editorial_candidates.limitation: The explicit characteristic formula already carries the proof; any figure should be schematic or use a clearly identified representative time.

editorial_candidates.source_claim: For f(u)=u^3 and Riemann states 1 to -1, the entropy profile is a shock 1 to -1/2 at speed 3/4, followed by a centered rarefaction on [-1,-1/2] and constant state -1; the flux prescription is the cubic arc then a chord (Statement lines 36–51).
editorial_candidates.why_warranted: Both the self-similar wave pattern and the nonconvex-flux concave-hull construction are geometric and otherwise require tracking several formulas.
editorial_candidates.content_to_draw_or_check: Use linked panels: x/t with regions x/t<3/4 (state 1), 3/4<x/t<3 (fan u=-sqrt((x/t)/3)), and x/t>3 (state -1), with shock ray x=3t/4; and f(u)=u^3 with the cubic arc on [-1,-1/2] joined to the chord from (-1/2,-1/8) to (1,1). Mark only the source-claimed states and interfaces; do not confuse the fan edge x=3t with a shock.
editorial_candidates.limitation: The profile and entropy verification are explicit; diagram is an optional reading aid.

editorial_candidates.source_claim: The piecewise-constant witness has states 0,-delta,+delta,0 separated by rays x=-delta t, x=0, x=delta t; all three satisfy Rankine–Hugoniot, but the middle stationary jump has positive Kruzhkov entropy production 2delta^2 (Statement lines 37–50; Given line 56).
editorial_candidates.why_warranted: A space-time partition makes the contrast between weak admissibility and the entropy failure at the middle ray immediate.
editorial_candidates.content_to_draw_or_check: Draw x horizontally and t vertically for t>0, three rays with slopes -delta,0,+delta, and label the four regions 0,-delta,+delta,0. Mark the central stationary interface and annotate weak jump residual zero on each ray versus positive entropy coefficient 2delta^2 only on x=0; show common zero initial trace. Do not present the non-entropy witness as the selected entropy solution.
editorial_candidates.limitation: A diagram is illustrative only; the piecewise formula and jump calculations establish the result.
